eligibility.quote: The program that runs on the UR controller reads too many bytes from the socket connection for setting digital outputs.  See [here](https://github.com/ros-industrial/universal_robot/blob/hydro-devel/ur_driver/prog#L226).  Most times this is not an issue because multiple commands are not typically in the socket buffer (the reference read command only returns the 2 values used for setting digital IO).

failed_conditions.quote: Ah, you're right. Seems number-of-bytes was specified, instead of number-of-items.

loudness.quote: This results in several `unrecognized command` messages being reported in the ROS log (although a more critical failure could be misinterpreting the data as a valid command).

resolution.quote: driver: sizeof(io_msgs) is 8 bytes, not 8 ints. Fix #107.

                 [pinnum] + 
                 [value]' with 'buf = struct.pack("!%ii" % len(params), *params)' (type + 2 integers; set_tool_voltage sends '[value] + 
 [0]'), while prog reads 'params_mult = socket_read_binary_integer(1+6+1)' for MSG_SET_DIGITAL_OUT — the message-size assumption crosses the PC/controller socket boundary, so stop at step 6 with interface kind 'wire protocol field'. Unit-boundary judgement (driverProg uploaded by driver.py but executing as a separate program on the UR controller) is defensible and flagged in the spec notes.
